extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark dataset consisting of 3,002 high-school geometry problems with dense descriptions in formal language, collected from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu. Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning. arXiv:2105.04165v3 [cs.CL], 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collect each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer from two popular textbooks for high school students.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data collected from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 by two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill, Geometryonline).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Hough Transformation is applied to extract geometry primitives (points, lines, arcs, and circles) from diagrams. Diagram symbols and text regions are extracted through RetinaNet object detector, and textual content is recognized by the optical character recognition tool MathPix. Symbol grounding is formulated as an optimization problem with geometric constraints.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each problem in Geometry3K is annotated with dense formal language descriptions that bridge the semantic gap between the textual and visual contents. Each problem data is labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A generated theorem application sequence is regarded as positive if the geometry solver Inter-GPS solves the problem after the application of that sequence. A positive sequence with the minimum length for a problem is seen as pseudo-optimal. After attempts, 1,501 training samples with the problem and its pseudo-optimal theorem application sequence were collected.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Educational level (high school or higher degree required for annotators)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work in this paper may inspire the following research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models and facilitate education.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Inter-GPS might not find a solution because of inaccurate parsing results and the incomplete theorem set. Diagram parsing tends to fail if there are ambiguous annotations or multiple primitives in the diagram. It is difficult for the text parser to handle nested expressions and uncertain references. The symbolic solver is still not capable of solving complex problems with combined shapes and shaded areas in the diagrams.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is designed for geometry problem solving tasks and evaluating algorithms' performance in symbolic reasoning and interpretable problem solving.
